_comment: SANITY CHECK: restormer_2 (pl_models/models/restormer_2.py, the unofficial Restormer) on 3T -> 7T (10_Pat_t1), 3 epochs per split, all 10 subject-level folds. restormer_2 is residual (output(fr) + x) so it now ends in Hardtanh(0, 1): source/target are slicify min-max normalised to [0, 1] and the IQA metrics use data_range=1.0. 'channels' must double at every level.

seed._comment: apply=true calls set_seed() before anything else: python/numpy/torch/cuda RNGs + cudnn.deterministic. Costs throughput (cudnn.benchmark is forced off).

prompts._comment: false skips the blocking 'logs/<exp> already exists, continue?' input(). Set false for unattended/queued runs. The 'slices not found' prompt in slice_checker.py is separate and always blocks.

model_info._comment: restormer_2.py takes num_blocks/num_heads/channels/num_refinement/expansion_factor (NOT restormer.py's dim/num_refinement_blocks/heads/bias/LayerNorm_type). The whole 'model' block is splatted into __init__ unfiltered, so the keys must match the signature exactly. output_range_01 says what range the MODEL speaks: true = [0, 1] (pair it with out_activation 'hardtanh'/'sigmoid'), false = [-1, 1] (pair it with 'tanh'). The pipeline itself is always [0, 1]; when false, master_half_slice_re.py::model_forward scales the input to [-1, 1] and the prediction back to [0, 1], so the loss, metrics and saved volumes are unchanged either way.
model_info.name: Restormer

direction._comment: 3T is the input, 7T the synthesis target; MASKS holds the binary brain masks. Filenames match exactly across all three directories, which slicify requires.

slicify._comment: Axial in-plane is 260x311, so pad_to must be >= 311; 320 pads to a square and keeps the in-plane scaling isotropic, then one 320->256 resize. Cache lands in <subjects_path>/slices/256x320/.

intensity_augmentations._comment: Only consumed when evaluation.ground_truth_norm == 'percentile'. [low_clip_value, high_percentile] passed to load_and_normalize_slices.

block_augments._comment: Pretext-task corruption of the model INPUT only (augmentations/block_augments_2d.py). Order is fixed: GIN -> blockwise downsample -> block mask.

tta_flips._comment: Flip-averaged inference (2^2 = 4 forward passes over H/W flips). Applies to the final evaluation and to sample_volume_during_training; never to training or validation loss. 'p' is unused by the 2D path.

augmentations._comment: Kornia 2D augmentation, rebuilt each epoch. Geometric transforms are drawn ONCE and shared by source/target/mask so the pair stays registered; erasing hits the input only; intensity_apply_to selects which side photometric jitter lands on ('source' | 'target' | 'both'). type='static' holds augmentation_prob fixed; 'dynamic' decays it linearly to 0 at epoch 'till', after which augmentation is off entirely.

loss._comment: types entries are [name, weight] or [name, weight, {constructor kwargs}]. A name must also appear in 'available' or compile_loss_fn raises. Use wavelet2D (not wavelet3D) for the slice pipeline. synth_seg_path is only read when 'SynthSeg' is active.

evaluation._comment: ground_truth_norm 'slicify' rebuilds the reference volume exactly the way patchify/slicify/slicify_nii.py built the cached target slices (mask, then a single global min-max) - this is what the model was trained against. 'percentile' is the legacy load_and_normalize_slices path and reads intensity_augmentations. slicify_percentile_clip must mirror the (currently commented-out) 0.995 clamp in slicify_nii.py; null = no clamp. weights_dir points evaluation at another run's checkpoint folder ('{split}' is replaced by the split index); null = this experiment's own.

fine_tunning._comment: Slice-pipeline weight init. pretrain_evaluate_only=true (with pretrain_boolean=true) forces epochs to 0, makes every subject a test subject, skips caching train/val slices, and scores pretrained_model_weight directly. Accepts bare state dicts and full training-state checkpoints.

finetunning._comment: Patch-pipeline spelling of the same thing; applied after fine_tunning, so it wins if both are set. Weights only - no optimizer/scheduler state.

resume_training._comment: Full-state resume: model, optimizer, scheduler, GradScaler, torch/cuda/python RNG and the split index. Requires a checkpoint written by the current LightningStyleCheckpoint (old bare state dicts are rejected). Training restarts at the stored epoch and splits before the stored split are skipped.

resume_from_sample._comment: Coarser skip: jump straight to split 'index' without loading anything. Also switches the average-metrics CSV to append mode.

training._comment: Optimizer: 'adam' or 'adamw' (default). lr_schedule.apply gates the scheduler entirely (false = constant learning_rate; it must gate construction, since LambdaLR's ctor performs an initial step()). When on, the LR schedule is a per-optimizer-step linear warmup over warmup_percentage_steps of total steps, optionally multiplied by a StepLR-style epoch decay - both folded into one LambdaLR so the checkpoint round-trips a single scheduler object. Gradients are clipped at max_norm=1.0. splits.num_test_samples sets the split size (num_splits = len(subjects) // num_test_samples); single_pass=true stops after split 0. mono_channel, num_workers, save_generation, scheduler: (unused).

checkpoint._comment: Two callbacks share this dir: top-k on val_loss and top-k on train_loss, both plus a periodic save. Files land as topk<monitor>_epoch=NN.pt and saveEvery_epoch_epoch=NN.pt, and every one of them is scored at the end. top_k=0 disables the heap and keeps only the periodic saves. save_dir, monitor, mode, filename_template: (unused - the driver hardcodes logs/<exp>/checkpoints/<split> and the monitors).

patch_inference._comment: (unused) 3D patch-pipeline aggregation settings, kept so this file matches its siblings.

device._comment: devices[0] is the single device everything runs on. cache_stratergy 'same_gpu' caches every slice tensor on that GPU up front (fastest, VRAM-hungry); anything else moves batches per step. accelerator, benchmark, strategy, cache_device_available: (unused).
